config.description: Jouw eigen ingediende items en, als beoordelaar, wat er op je wacht.
config._note: mijn-hr-self-service: smallest useful ADR-001 menu-1 dashboard — 3 @me-scoped stat KPIs (mine), 2 approver stat KPIs (per ADR-001 Rule 2, the manager self-service surface, deep-linking to the existing TimesheetApproval/ExpenseApproval pages), 1 @me-scoped object-table of recent timesheets. All six widgets are from the built-in widget enum (stat, object-table) — no custom widgets, no dateRange, no charts; growth belongs to a later dashboard change.

config.description: Ingediende urenstaten die wachten op goedkeuring of afkeuring.

config._note: HR/labour approval record (urenstaat). A single Timesheet captures the hours an employee logged for one period plus a submit -> approve/reject -> reopen approval workflow (x-openregister-lifecycle on `status`). ADR-062 round-2 rework: (1) total-hours KPI stat top-left so the approver sees the claimed volume at a glance; (2) the data widget SPLIT into 'Time entry' (period/description/project/cost centre/billable -- what was worked) and 'Approval' (status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason -- the workflow trail), each excluding employeeId since the Related panel already resolves and links the claiming Employee by name; (3) related alongside both, matching their combined height. Files sits full-width below for approval evidence and signed timesheets (approval documents matter, so they are on the body, not a tab). NO email/calendar/talk widgets -- the Timesheet schema declares no comms linkedTypes and a labour record does not correspond; any communication is with the person (Employee), not the record. lifecycleActions expose the schema's own submit/approve/reject/reopen transitions (guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard). Audit history is pushed to a sidebar tab as a rarely-scanned surface.

config.description: Ingediende declaraties die wachten op goedkeuring of afkeuring.

config._note: Expense-reimbursement claim (onkostendeclaratie). A single Expense holds one claim (amount / currency / category / date + attached receipt) and a submit -> approve/reject -> reimburse lifecycle (x-openregister-lifecycle on `status`). Content starts at gridY 0 with the 'Claim' data (title/description/amount/currency/category/expenseDate/receiptFile) then 'Approval' (status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason/reimbursedAt) below it, both excluding employeeId since Related already resolves the claiming Employee by name; an amount KPI stat sits top-right so the payout figure is unmissable, with Related beneath it matching the combined left-column height. The Files widget (receipt / bon) runs full-width AFTER the domain cards, same placement convention as Timesheet's approval evidence -- the approver reads the claim record first, then opens the receipt to verify it. NO email/calendar/talk -- Expense declares no comms linkedTypes; a reimbursement claim is a financial/HR record, not a correspondence thread. lifecycleActions expose submit/approve/reject/reimburse (approve/reject guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard; reimburse is terminal). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

Hub archetype: Employee is the record every other HR/payroll schema in hrmq points AT (EmploymentContract.employeeId, Payslip.employeeId, Timesheet.employeeId, Expense.employeeId — all now canonical $ref relations, ADR-062 rule 7), so the page's job is to be the single place an HR/payroll admin lands to see one person's whole labour and pay picture. ADR-062 round-2 rework: the data widget is SPLIT into 'Person' (employeeNumber/firstName/lastName/dateOfBirth/bsn — the identity attributes) at 8-wide beside an in-grid stats-block (KPIs, top-right — replaces the deprecated summaryAggregates header chips) at 4-wide; 'Employment & compliance' (startDate/endDate/grossMonthlySalary/taxTableColor/ID-document retention/30%-ruling/A1 posting/jurisdiction-specific onboarding flags — 18 fields, genuinely this schema's bulk) runs full-width below since it has no natural width-4 partner. Contracts and Timesheets are paired FK-scoped lists, then Payslips (allowCreate:false — payroll-generated, not hand-created from here) and Expenses, then a Files leaf for the personnel file (justified by identityDocumentVerified/identityDocumentRetainedUntil/loonheffingenVerklaringOnFile — real statutory document-retention fields on this schema, not a generic add). NO calendar/contacts/talk: Employee declares no appointment or comms linkedType — the person's own identity data lives on this record, it is not a link to a separate NC contact. No lifecycleActions — Employee carries no x-openregister-lifecycle. Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

Leaf compliance record: no other schema in hrmq references EmploymentContract by FK, so the page is a simple two-panel layout -- the data widget (type/writtenContract/dates/hoursPerWeek/hourlyWage/cao/awfTariff plus the jurisdiction-specific fields: workingTimeDocumented, overtimeMultiplier, ftePartOfYearMinijob, dpaeFiledBeforeStart) at 8-wide, excluding employeeId since the Related panel already resolves and links the owning Employee by name -- and Related at 4-wide for that one meaningful outbound ref. No child lists (nothing points at a contract), no files/calendar/comms leaves (no linkedType or document field evidence on this schema), no lifecycleActions (EmploymentContract has no x-openregister-lifecycle). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

Financial-document archetype (x-schema-org: schema:Invoice), same family as Expense's amount-first design: three headline tiles (gross pay, net pay, Related-to-Employee) lead the page since that is what an employee or approver checks first, followed by the dense data widget carrying the full gross-to-net withholding breakdown (NL loonheffing/zvw/wkr, DE Lohnsteuer/Soli/Kirchensteuer, FR cotisations/PAS, US FICA/Medicare -- the schema is genuinely multi-jurisdiction: only one jurisdiction's fields populate per real record, but which one varies per payslip so a static manifest cannot cherry-pick per-instance; all fields surface via one widget, sized to its true field count and set to 4 columns full-width rather than clipped at 2). ADR-062 round-2: data widget now excludes employeeId (resolved via Related instead of raw uuid) and the height budget was corrected from the round-1 h7 (which clipped ~54 fields behind a scrollbar) to match content. Stat format uses 'number' not 'currency' because Payslip.currency varies per record (EUR/USD) and a widget's format is static. No files/calendar/comms leaves: nothing in the schema models an attachable payslip document or appointment, and Payslip carries no x-openregister-lifecycle so there are no lifecycleActions. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

Batch/reconciliation archetype: a PayrollRun is a per-period aggregate of an administration's payslips, so its page leads with the GL-reconciliation totals (totalGross/totalNet/withholdingLiabilityBalance -- exactly the numbers xc-payroll-gl-reconciliation and xc-withholding-liability-clearing check) as stat KPIs, then the full record (period/administrationId/jurisdiction/status/glLiabilityPosted/glExpensePosted/withholdingsClearedToZero) in the data widget below. NO Payslip child list and NO related panel: Payslip carries no payrollRunId (or any) FK back to PayrollRun in the schema, and administrationId is a bare string, not a resolvable object reference -- adding either would fabricate a relation the schema does not carry. NO lifecycleActions: `status` is a plain enum (draft/approved/posted/paid) with no `x-openregister-lifecycle` transition map on this schema, unlike Timesheet/Expense -- driving lifecycleActions here would invent transition names the backend does not guard. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Wage-tax / social-security filings by period and statutory deadline.

config._note: Statutory-deadline archetype: a filing's whole purpose is 'was it filed on time and is proof retained'. loonaangifte-filing-lifecycle (2026-07-12) gave NL filings a real create->review->confirm->send workflow, so the page now leads with a compact status/tijdvakcode/deadline/response widget (fi-status) before the full filing data widget, and exposes the klaarzetten/bevestigen/verzenden/heropenen/corrigeren transitions via lifecycleActions (Timesheet pattern). No stats-block KPI tile is used for Status/Deadline: the vendored app-manifest-v2 schema's stat/stats-block `metric` only supports count/sum aggregation, which cannot echo a non-numeric field (enum/date) of the current object, so fi-status is a `data` widget instead -- schema-valid and functionally equivalent (prominent, top-of-page). No related panel (the schema carries no employeeId/administrationId or any other object-FK -- a filing is an organisation-level record, not scoped to a person). Files is included full-width for the filed submission/deposit proof, justified by the schema's own retainedUntil/furnishedToRecipientDate/filedWithAuthorityDate retention-evidence fields (NL 7yr / DE 6yr / US 4yr retention obligations). No calendar/comms leaves -- deadline is a plain date field, not an appointment/event linkedType. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: UPA (Uniforme Pensioenaangifte) deliveries by period and sector fund, gated on the referenced payroll run's approval.

config._note: pension-filing-upa-mvp (2026-07-12): same statutory-filing shape as LoonaangifteFilingDetail (create->review->confirm->send, gated on an external precondition), but this schema ALSO carries a real FK (payrollRunId -> PayrollRun, the run the delivery reports on), so the layout follows the TimesheetDetail split instead: pf-status leads top-left with the prominent status/deadline/response facts, pf-related sits top-right at matching height to resolve and link the referenced PayrollRun, then pf-data runs below with the remaining record fields (period/fund/aanleverkenmerk/verzondenDoor), excluding payrollRunId since Related already resolves it. Same reasoning as loonaangifte for NOT using a stats-block: the vendored app-manifest-v2 schema's stat/stats-block `metric` only supports count/sum aggregation over a collection, which cannot echo a non-numeric field (enum/date) of the current object, so pf-status is a `data` widget instead -- schema-valid and functionally equivalent (prominent, top-of-page). No Files leaf: unlike LoonaangifteFiling, PensionFiling carries no retention/proof-of-filing fields (no retainedUntil/furnishedToRecipientDate equivalent) -- the response is captured in-record (responseStatus/responseMessage), not as an attached document. No calendar/comms leaves -- deadline is a plain date field, not an appointment/event linkedType. lifecycleActions expose controleren/bevestigen/verzenden/heropenen/corrigeren, controleren guarded server-side by PayrollRunApprovedGuard. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Payroll-to-GL posting attempts: one balanced loonjournaalpost handed off to shillinq per approved loonrun.

config._note: payroll-glpost-shillinq (2026-07-12): a PayrollGLPost is hrmq's log of ONE handoff attempt into shillinq's JournalEntry register -- never the journal itself (design.md D1). TimesheetDetail/PensionFilingDetail split: pg-status leads top-left with the prominent outcome facts (status/postedAt/errorMessage), pg-related sits top-right to resolve and link the referenced PayrollRun (a real $ref, unlike journalEntryId), then pg-data runs below with the remaining record fields including the journalNumber/journalEntryId pointer into shillinq (plain display only -- no cross-app deep link in MVP, per design.md's 'posted != materialised' risk note) and the lines snapshot. NO lifecycleActions: status has no x-openregister-lifecycle transition map -- PayrollGLPostService drives every transition server-side from `occ hrmq:glpost:run`, exactly the PayrollRunDetail precedent (never invent a user-facing transition the backend does not guard). No Files/calendar/comms leaves -- this is a system-generated audit record, not a document or event. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Ingediende verlofaanvragen die wachten op goedkeuring of afkeuring.

config._note: leave-verzuim-mvp (2026-07-12): drives the EXISTING LeaveRequest lifecycle from portal-schemas (submit -> approve/reject, guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard) -- nothing on the schema changes here, only its UI. TimesheetDetail pattern: the data widget is SPLIT into 'Request' (leaveType/startDate/endDate/hours/reason -- what is being requested) and 'Approval' (status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason -- the workflow trail), both excluding employeeId since Related already resolves and links the requesting Employee by name. Files sits full-width below for supporting documents (e.g. a bijzonder-verlof invitation). NO stat KPI tile: unlike Timesheet's hours-sum or Expense's amount-sum, a leave request has no single numeric headline worth a dedicated stat (hours is optional and nullable). lifecycleActions expose exactly submit/approve/reject -- no invented cancel/withdraw edge (PayrollRunDetail _note precedent: never claim a transition the backend does not guard). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Verlofsaldi per medewerker, jaar en type: toegekende, bovenwettelijke en gebruikte uren, plus het berekende resterende saldo.
Ziektegevallen en de Wet-verbetering-poortwachter-mijlpalen (administratieve gegevens, geen medische gegevens).

config._note: leave-verzuim-mvp (2026-07-12): administrative-only sickness case -- NO medical/diagnosis data exists on this schema or its widgets (REQ-VWP-002). The 'Case' data widget (firstSickDay/recoveredDate/status/wachtdag/loondoorbetalingPercentage) excludes employeeId since Related already resolves and links the sick Employee by name; the 'Poortwachter milestones' widget surfaces all eight Due/Done WVP dates (probleemanalyse/plan van aanpak/UWV 42-wekenmelding/eerstejaarsevaluatie) so the re-integration clock is the page's second headline fact. Files is labeled and described for gespreksverslagen & plan-van-aanpak process documents ONLY -- repeating the no-medical-data warning, matching the schema's own privacy stance. lifecycleActions expose exactly herstellen/heropenen (gemeld<->hersteld) -- no invented edges. Audit history is a sidebar tab.
